A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the first time, we present a thermodynamically consistent equation of state of a system of interacting fermions with momentum-dependent interaction in anisotropic momentum distributions.
the anisotropy of the momentum distribution is a significant factor in determining the phase diagram of the deconfinement.
the deconfinement temperature is lowered by the anisotropy of nuclear matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase boundary of the transition is strongly affected by the anisotropy in the momentum distribution of the colliding nuclei.
the phase diagram for anisotropic nuclear matter is qualitatively similar to that for isotropic nuclear matter, but the phase transition is shifted to higher baryon density and temperature.
the anisotropic momentum-distribution in the nuclear matter leads to a phase transition at a lower value of temperature and baryon chemical potential than that in isotropic nuclear matter.
